linkedin.title: This Week in Finance & Tech
linkedin.body:
Britain is beginning one of its largest electricity grid overhauls in generations. The project requires thousands of miles of new power lines to meet climate goals, though it comes with the trade-off of higher short-term energy bills and local opposition. Meanwhile, questions persist regarding the argument that removing pollution limits for US power plants will lower costs or have minimal climate impact.

In the tech sector, Apple has unveiled its new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. For those interested in the startup ecosystem, TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is focusing on scaling challenges, with sessions on moving from prototype to production. On the consumer front, smart bird feeders equipped with cameras and dedicated apps are gaining popularity.

Scientific developments this week include NASA and IBM making their lunar mapping tools open source. In more experimental research, scientists have attempted to replace parts of a mouse's cortex with human brain cells, though the results showed only modest improvements. For EV owners, experts note that battery degradation is usually a gradual process, so changes in vehicle behavior are often better indicators of battery health than the age of the car alone.

story_card.headline: A new wild cat species found in Bolivia
story_card.standfirst: Scientists have officially identified a tiny new feline in the country's cloud forests.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Researchers identified a previously unknown species of wild cat living in Bolivia's Yungas forest.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: The cat was discovered in the cloud forest. It is smaller than the average house cat.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: This is the first time in over 100 years that a new living feline species has been named.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Look for future studies on the population size and conservation needs of this rare cat.

story_card.caption:
Scientists have identified a brand new species of wild cat in the Bolivian cloud forest.

This tiny feline is smaller than your average house cat and lives deep within the Yungas forest. It is a rare scientific milestone, marking the first time in over a century that a new living cat species has been officially described.
